evidence: Purpose-built collateral-unboundedness probe found no previously-bounded shape that became unbounded, watchdogs on both def and async def lanes.
R11-05, the one finding that claimed otherwise, is REFUTED on an `after:` control that behaves identically at the same delays on every prior commit.
Exactly one stable PASS->FAIL delta across 163 gate checks and 527 sweep scripts, and it is our own test encoding the #206 rule #212 deliberately reverses.
did_212_reopen_a_bounded_cycle_class.caveat: #212 opened no SEMANTIC hole but made a pre-existing RESOURCE defect unbounded: R11-04, +455 MB / 24 s at 200 machines, strictly linear, no plateau.

evidence: R11-01 (filed Blocker) REFUTED: an attacker who can edit `version` can equally edit `state_ids` and land in the target state directly. from_snapshot is a documented trusted-input boundary (#205); machine_hash is a fingerprint, not a MAC. from_snapshot(minimum_version=3) raises SnapshotVersionError on the forged blob.

R11-03 (filed High) REFUTED: control V1, the only vector reachable from the documented public API, is correctly refused with UnknownEventError. V2 needs non-exported modules; V3/V4 need an already-held genuine engine event; V5 needs blob-write, which reaches the target state with no event at all.
R11-02 (filed High) DOWNGRADED to Low: equivalent-doors probe shows forging `configuration` alone reaches the same state with no event.
did_v3_or_v2_upcast_reopen_the_195_203_f.pattern: Third consecutive round in which a Blocker filed against engine-event provenance was refuted by our own control probe. Adopted as a TRIAGE PRECONDITION: any finding whose threat model requires blob-write must first be tested against 'what does the same writer achieve with state_ids/context alone?'

new_issues.title: `_timer_handles` grows by one retained entry per `raise(delay=)` beat and is never pruned - an unbounded leak on the heartbeat shape #212 just made legal
#215's `_descent_done` gate: an entry action that awaits its own receipt hangs `start()` forever, silently
#216 validates the root config only: a misspelled key inside a state is silently dropped, with no raise and no warning, even under `strict_config=True`
Restore then re-persist without `start()` silently drops every armed delayed self-send - #213's own failure mode, one hop later
A `RunawayChainError` chain trip reaches only `last_error`, and the next benign event erases it - a permanently inert machine reports healthy

raised_as_notes_not_issues.note: snapshot guide should recommend minimum_version=3, not 1, now that v3 carries provenance
scheduled_sends does not get the strict check pending_events does; a chart upgrade that undeclares an event yields silent delivery. Fix: route _rearm_restored_self_sends through _admit_restored
on_invalid_event is structurally unreachable on the restore path; from_snapshot takes no plugins=. The library's own pin registers the plugin after the restore and asserts only on last_error
structure_hash omits raise(delay=) delays although it covers after delays; delay 60000 -> 100 leaves the hash byte-identical
lane is persisted but unenforceable on the sync engine (no priority queue by construction)
the #210 changelog sentence conflates two plateaus: descent-seeded is maxIterations+3, externally kicked is exactly +2. Swept limits {3,5,7,9}
SimulatedClock fires neither after nor restored scheduled_sends, so callers cannot unit-test restored deadlines under virtual time
